key_findings.finding: Directly relevant primary study exists: PMID 25097016, “Human papillomavirus 16/18 E7 viral loads predict distant metastasis in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma” (J Clin Virol, 2014). In 312 oral cavity SCC patients (not oropharynx), quantitative PCR-measured HPV-16/18 E7 load ≥15.0 copies/genome was independently associated with 5-year distant metastasis in multivariable analysis. High viral load combined with adverse features defined risk groups; the high-risk group had a 74% 5-year distant-metastasis rate, intermediate group 17%, and low-risk group 1%. Abstract does not provide separate hazard ratios or separate HPV-16 versus HPV-18 effect estimates; it reports both thresholds as independent risk factors. This supports prediction of distant metastasis, not a specifically reported lung-metastasis or metastatic-recurrence endpoint.

source_tools.relevance: Initial search identified the directly relevant primary study and abstract-level results.
Fetched abstract verifies cohort, oral cavity population, assay and cutoff, multivariable association, and 5-year distant-metastasis risk strata.
Follow-up exact-phrase search was performed; unrelated lung/oral metastasis case reports were not primary evidence for this association.
